text:
Alex: Quick follow-up from today’s All-hands — pricing/packaging Qs that popped up. I'll collect answers here. First: what’s the overage / grace policy for monthly credits? @Paula @Jordan
Paula: Short answer: we give a 5% grace buffer on hosted monthly credits for self-serve accounts, and we notify at 80% / 95% / 100% via email + console. Billing for overage is per-token at the published overage rate and appears on the next invoice. For enterprise contracts we can negotiate different buffers and billing cadence.
Mira: Follow-up: do credits expire at month end or after 30 days?
Paula: Credits are monthly and reset at the UTC month boundary unless promo terms specify otherwise. Pilot / grant credits have explicit expiry dates shown in the console.
Sanjay: Clarify rate limits vs quotas — are they enforced at the account or API-key level? We have infra that still uses the main org key.
Jordan: Defaults are per-API-key rate limits and per-account quotas. We strongly recommend separate keys for internal tooling. We’ll add SDK snippets in the docs showing how to scope keys per-service.
Alex: Will there be per-route quotas? e.g., separate limits for embeddings vs chat generation so a spike in embeddings doesn't kill chat.
Mira: Yes — console supports per-route quotas today for Dedicated & Private. Hosted will get routed quotas (per-model/per-route) in the next quarter release.
Jordan: Also: we're rolling out a short burst allowance — small bursts beyond the configured rate limit if capacity exists, with behavior dependent on plan tier.
Paula: How does billing for bursts work?
Paula: Bursts are metered as normal usage. There's no extra "burst fee" — but sustained bursts that exceed monthly credits will count as overage on the next invoice. We also send alerts so teams can act before an invoice surprises them.
Sanjay: If bursts are dropped due to capacity, what do apps see? 429s or queued requests?
Mira: Behavior depends on tier: higher tiers get graceful queuing up to a soft-latency SLO; free/self-serve may see immediate 429s once hard limits are hit. We'll document exact thresholds and expected latency windows.
Alex: A couple of quick action items from this thread: @Mira to publish a Pricing FAQ with examples, @Sanjay to add SDK key-scoping samples and a snippet to auto-retry vs backoff on 429s, @Paula to add an invoice worked example showing overage math.
Paula: I'll prepare an invoice example showing line items for base usage, credits applied, bursts, and overage calculations.
Jordan: We'll update the Console > Billing roadmap note by EOD next Tuesday and add a short blurb about enterprise-customized rate limits and SLAs. Enterprise deals can request custom quotas and grace terms during contracting.
Mira: Linking the meeting notes here (internal placeholder): https://internal.redwood/notes/pricing-allhands-03-23 — converting to public docs + FAQ this week.
Alex: Thanks all — I'll keep this thread open until the docs and examples are live. :thumbsup:
